_about: WORDS THREE, HIS HOMEWORK, SHEET FIVE: YOUR RULES, ON THE BIGGEST MOUTHS (VAMILY rules 466(f), 467, 465; ask rows 629, 637). Made better by his sheets one and two: every card names the rule of HIS it tests, on the card itself, so he can answer it fast: THEY CURSE (rule 467: where a real person would, and where they would not), NO BATTERY COUNT IN A FEELING (his NO on 2.2), SAY IT LIKE A PERSON (his NOs on 2.5 and 2.6), NO FASHION NAMES AS A JOKE (his NO on 2.1), PLAIN BEATS CLEVER (his lines), THE DANGER STAYS DARK (his starred old woman). The lines come from the mouths with the most lines (his men in a fight, the survivor after, the job board, the why line, the feed), so his answers teach the most lines at once. No card asks again what he already ruled in the same spot. tools/bohemia_words_two_homework.js reads every line out of the named file; nothing here is a line. Nothing he writes goes into the game until he says he is done (rule 465).
said: you show me one sentence or one dialog caption that you made and then I'll tell you how I want that shit to sound

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: a calm old hand when a man drops
cards.mouth: YOUR MAN, WHEN ONE OF YOURS DROPS
cards.who_plain: The oldest man in your crew
cards.when: one of your men goes down in the middle of a fight
cards.where: in a FIGHT, over his head
cards.teaches: THEY CURSE, THE EDGE: your own 'DESI! FUCK!' was a friend; this is the calm veteran giving an order as a man drops; does even he curse

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: raiders at your own place
cards.mouth: THE ENEMY'S LEADER, AT YOUR PLACE
cards.role: leads the crew that came for your place
cards.who_plain: The leader of a crew raiding your own place
cards.when: they come over your wall and the fight opens
cards.where: on the card that opens a FIGHT at your place
cards.expect: Your place has what we need
cards.teaches: THEY CURSE, THE WHY LINE: 163 why lines and none curse; your enemy line did ('fuck faces'); does every armed man say it that way, or only some

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: a bar owner who was robbed
cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: The woman who runs the bar with no sign
cards.when: you ask what her job is and what it pays
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.teaches: THEY CURSE ON THE JOB BOARD: your old woman did not curse; an angry bar owner sending you after a man who stiffed her might; 102 job lines hang on it

cards.rule: THEY CURSE: a little girl trapped in a drain
cards.who_plain: A little girl stuck in a storm drain, with rain coming
cards.when: you hear her from the street
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that stops your crew on the road
cards.teaches: THEY CURSE, THE YOUNGEST: rule 467 says a kid begging curses the way a real kid would; this one is small and about to drown; and does she cry out in Spanish

cards.rule: NO BATTERY COUNT IN A FEELING: money in grief
cards.who_plain: The man in your crew who only thinks about money
cards.when: you win a fight and one of your men died in it
cards.where: on the screen after a FIGHT
cards.teaches: NO BATTERY COUNT IN A FEELING, THE EDGE: your NO on 2.2 killed money talk in joy; this is a greedy man talking money over a dead friend, on purpose, to be cold; does it stay or go

cards.rule: NO BATTERY COUNT IN A FEELING: happy, said right?
cards.who_plain: The cook who lost her kitchen to the boss called THE POT
cards.when: you come back after you killed the boss who took her kitchen
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card after a boss falls
cards.teaches: SCARY HAPPY WITHOUT THE COUNT: the same moment as your NO on 2.2, said with no payment in it; is this what happy sounds like, or is something still off (it is not scary first)

cards.rule: SAY IT LIKE A PERSON: a clerk's errand
cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: The clerk of a tower town
cards.when: you ask what his job is and what it pays
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.expect: A sealed letter goes to the council
cards.teaches: SAY IT LIKE A PERSON, THE EDGE: your NOs on 2.5 and 2.6 killed committee English; this man IS a clerk and talks like one ('signed for inside six days', 'the seal is the receipt'); is that his person, or is it the same slop

cards.rule: SAY IT LIKE A PERSON: an old soldier's order
cards.mouth: A SIDE QUEST ON THE ROAD
cards.who_plain: An old soldier telling your crew how a hard thing is done
cards.when: something has to be killed and nobody wants to do it
cards.where: on the MAP, on a side quest's card
cards.teaches: SAY IT LIKE A PERSON: a list and a moral ('the correct way to do a thing you don't want to feel'); is that how an old soldier talks, or is it writing

cards.rule: SAY IT LIKE A PERSON: an official voice on the feed
cards.who_plain: The Network's own page, the people who keep the internet on
cards.when: it is night and the Network posts its notice
cards.teaches: SAY IT LIKE A PERSON, THE OTHER EDGE: this is meant to sound like an office, calm and wrong ('Family abroad is safe'); is a voice that is not a person allowed when it is the creepy part, or is it slop too

cards.rule: NO FASHION NAMES AS A JOKE: and clothes jokes?
cards.who_plain: The man in your crew who cares about clothes
cards.where: on the screen after a FIGHT
cards.teaches: NO FASHION NAMES AS A JOKE, THE EDGE: no brand in this one, only a clothes joke from a man who cares about clothes (the runway is in the game's look); is a clothes joke dead too, or only the names

cards.rule: PLAIN BEATS CLEVER: a quip after a win
cards.role: after a fight with a road crew
cards.when: you win a fight against raiders who stopped your crew on the road
cards.where: on the screen after a FIGHT
cards.teaches: PLAIN BEATS CLEVER, THE EDGE: you starred the cruel boots joke and turned 'out of spite' into plain words; this is a short quip with a pun ('Paid in full'); does a quip live

cards.rule: THE DANGER STAYS DARK: a man who explains the beast
cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: A professor who dug the fossil beds before the crash
cards.when: you ask what his job is and what it pays
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.expect: The lab grew one ground sloth
cards.teaches: THE DANGER STAYS DARK, THE EDGE: your starred old woman never explained the 'dark shadows'; this man knows exactly what the beast is and where its bones were found; may the one who knows explain it
